correctness.rationale: Unitary reflection splits H into an irreducible tridiagonal even block B_(m+1) and a real-symmetric odd path A_(m−1). Determinant recursion yields (z²+γ²−4)U_(m−1)(z/2)². The even tridiagonal eigenvector is determined by its first coordinate, so it has exactly one Jordan block at each eigenvalue. The simple U roots μ_j=2cos(πj/m) coincide with moving roots ±sqrt(4−γ²) precisely at specified subthreshold γ. At γ=2 both moving roots collide at zero with the odd path root iff m even. Jordan exponential establishes matching upper/lower norm powers. Independent exact symbolic characteristic-polynomial and γ=2 nullity calculations for m=2,…,7 corroborate, but the tridiagonal argument proves all m.

value.rationale: Provides the crucial physically observable distinction between a real spectrum and a bounded propagator: subthreshold embedded Jordan defects cause linear amplification. The even/odd m jump at γ=2 supplies an exact design boundary for non-Hermitian lattice dynamics.

final_claim: For a 2m-site zero-flux uniform ring with opposite ±iγ and m≥2, the exact subthreshold defective strengths are 2sin(πk/m) for 1≤k< m/2, with two embedded J2⊕J1 eigenspaces and Θ(t) growth. At γ=2 the zero Jordan block is J2 for odd m or J3⊕J1 for even m, giving Θ(t) or Θ(t²); for γ>2 growth is exponential.
